1 طَلِحَتِ الإِبِلُ , (S, A,) [aor.
طَلَحَ ,] inf. n. طَلَحٌ, (TA,) The camels had a complaint (S, A) of their bellies (S) from eating of the trees called طَلْح. (S, A. [But see إِبِلٌ.]) ―
-b2- And طَلِحَ, aor.
طَلَحَ , (K,) inf. n. as above, (TK,) He (a man, TK,) was, or became, empty, or void of food, in his belly; as also طُلِحَ, like عُنِىَ. (K.) ＝
-A2- طَلَحَ, (S, M, A, K,) aor.
طَلَحَ , inf. n. طَلْحٌ and طَلَاحَةٌ, (M, K,) said of a camel, (S, M, A, K,) He was, or became, lean, or emaciated, by reason of fatigue, or of disease: (A:) or fatigued, or wearied: (ISk, S, K:) or injured, or hurt, by fatigue: (AZ, T, TA:) or he was, or became, fatigued, and fell down by reason of travel: (M, TA:) or طَلِحَ, aor.
طَلَحَ , inf. n. طَلَحٌ; and طَلَحَ, aor.
طَلَحَ , inf. n. طَلْحٌ; he was, or became, fatigued: or lean, by reason of fatigue, or of disease. (MA.) ―
-b2- And طَلَحَ, inf. n. طَلَاحٌ, (tropical:) He (a man) was, or became, bad, corrupt, or vicious. (A, L. [See طَلَاحٌ below.]) ＝
-A3- طَلَحَهُ, aor.
طَلَحَ , [inf. n. طَلْحٌ,] He, or it, (a man, MA, Msb, or journeying, A,) rendered him lean, or emaciated him; (A, MA, Msb;) namely, a camel: (A, Msb:) [or] he fatigued him; (MA, K;) i. e., a camel; (S, K;) and (K) so ↓ اطلحهُ ; and ↓ طلّحهُ , (S, K,) inf. n. of the latter تَطْلِيحٌ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
